notes:
Great news! The package `xyzservices` is [officially supported](https://pyodide.org/en/stable/usage/packages-in-pyodide.html) in the latest Pyodide release used by PyScript.

To use it in PyScript simply add it to the `packages` section of your TOML configuration like this:

```
packages = ["xyzservices" ]
```

Or if you're using a JSON configuration, like this:

```
{
    packages: ["xyzservices"]
 }
```

Read more about using packages in PyScript [in our documentation](https://docs.pyscript.net/latest/user-guide/configuration/#packages).

examples.title: Explore Providers
examples.code:
""" A first look at xyzservices. xyzservices is a lightweight catalog of XYZ raster tile providers (the basemaps you see behind interactive maps). It ships a single JSON database and a Python API for browsing and using each provider. Docs: https://xyzservices.readthedocs.io/ """ from IPython.core.display import display, HTML import xyzservices import xyzservices.providers as xyz heading("Browsing the provider catalog") note( "The xyzservices.providers module is a " "Bunch (an enhanced dict) of tile providers. " "Top-level keys are families like CartoDB, OpenStreetMap, " "Esri, and so on." ) # Top-level provider families. Many entries are themselves Bunches # containing several variants (e.g., CartoDB.Positron, CartoDB.Voyager). families = sorted(xyz.keys()) note(f"There are {len(families)} provider families. " f"A sample: {', '.join(families[:8])}, ...") # Pick a single, free, no-token-needed provider to inspect. positron = xyz.CartoDB.Positron note("A TileProvider is a dict-like object with the " "metadata you need to actually request tiles:") display(HTML( f"
    " f"
  • name: {positron.name}
    • " f"
  • url template: {positron.url}
    • " f"
  • attribution: {positron.html_attribution}
    • " f"
  • max zoom: {positron.max_zoom}
    • " f"
" ), append=True) heading("Building a real tile URL", level=3) note( "The build_url method fills in the " "{x}, {y}, {z} and any " "provider-specific placeholders (like {variant} " "or {r} for retina)." ) # Tile coordinates for roughly central London at zoom 6. tile_url = positron.build_url(x=32, y=21, z=6) display(HTML(f"{tile_url}"), append=True)

examples.title: Tokens And Filtering
examples.code:
# --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Filtering the catalog and handling providers that need API tokens. # --------------------------------------------------------------------- import xyzservices import xyzservices.providers as xyz heading("Which providers are free to use right now?") note( "Some providers (Mapbox, Thunderforest, Stadia, ...) require an " "API key. requires_token() tells you whether a " "TileProvider still has unfilled placeholders like " "<insert your access token here>." ) # `xyz.flatten()` walks the nested Bunch and yields a flat dict of # {dotted_name: TileProvider}. Perfect for filtering. all_providers = xyz.flatten() note(f"Total tile provider entries: {len(all_providers)}") token_free = { name: tp for name, tp in all_providers.items() if not tp.requires_token() } needs_token = { name: tp for name, tp in all_providers.items() if tp.requires_token() } note( f"Free out of the box: {len(token_free)}. " f"Need an API key: {len(needs_token)}." ) # Show a handful of providers that need a token, so you know what to # look out for. sample_locked = list(needs_token.keys())[:6] display(HTML( "Examples requiring a token:
    " + "".join(f"
  • {n}
    • " for n in sample_locked) + "
" ), append=True) heading("Supplying a token", level=3) note( "TileProviders are dict-like, so you fill in placeholders by " "assignment. Below we plug a fake token into a copy of the " "Stadia AlidadeSmooth provider; in real use you'd paste your " "own key." ) stadia = xyz.Stadia.AlidadeSmooth.copy() note(f"Before: requires_token() = {stadia.requires_token()}") stadia["api_key"] = "my-fake-token-1234" note(f"After: requires_token() = {stadia.requires_token()}") # Once the token is set, build_url returns a fully usable URL. example_url = stadia.build_url(x=8, y=5, z=4) display(HTML(f"{example_url}"), append=True) heading("Searching by attribution", level=3) note("Find every OpenStreetMap-derived provider in the catalog:") osm_based = sorted( name for name, tp in all_providers.items() if "OpenStreetMap" in tp.get("attribution", "") ) note(f"Matches: {len(osm_based)}. First ten:") display(HTML("
    " + "".join(f"
  1. {n}
    2. " for n in osm_based[:10]) + "
"), append=True)

examples.title: Render A Basemap
examples.code: # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Use xyzservices URLs to actually fetch and assemble a small basemap. # --------------------------------------------------------------------- import io import numpy as np import matplotlib.pyplot as plt from PIL import Image import requests import xyzservices import xyzservices.providers as xyz heading("Stitching a basemap from XYZ tiles") note( "We'll pick a token-free provider, ask xyzservices for tile " "URLs over a small grid, fetch each 256x256 PNG, and paste " "them into one image. This is the same idea libraries like " "contextily use under the hood." ) # A clean, light basemap that doesn't need an API key. provider = xyz.CartoDB.Positron note(f"Using provider: {provider.name}") # Pick a 3x3 grid of tiles at zoom 4 covering western Europe-ish. zoom = 4 x_range = range(7, 10) y_range = range(5, 8) tile_size = 256 mosaic = Image.new( "RGB", (tile_size * len(x_range), tile_size * len(y_range)), "white", ) # build_url is the right way to materialize a URL: it substitutes # {x}/{y}/{z} plus any provider-specific bits like {r} or {s}. fetched = 0 for ix, x in enumerate(x_range): for iy, y in enumerate(y_range): url = provider.build_url(x=x, y=y, z=zoom) response = requests.get( url, headers={"User-Agent": "xyzservices-pyscript-example"}, timeout=10, ) response.raise_for_status() tile = Image.open(io.BytesIO(response.content)).convert("RGB") mosaic.paste(tile, (ix * tile_size, iy * tile_size)) fetched += 1 note(f"Fetched and stitched {fetched} tiles.") fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 6)) ax.imshow(np.asarray(mosaic)) ax.set_xticks([]) ax.set_yticks([]) ax.set_title(f"{provider.name} @ z={zoom}") fig.tight_layout() display(fig, append=True) # Always show the attribution -- it's required by most providers. note(f"Tiles © {provider.html_attribution}")
